_comment: Context-driven NPC talk (NPCConversation II.8 LIFE TALK). Every pool here is picked only when its condition holds for the speaker: family, jobs, travel, wars, the Goblin Horde, elections, fights, games. Placeholders are filled from the speaker's life record before the {a|b} alternation is resolved; {a} and {b} in scripts are the two speakers.

familyPartner: {I should bring|Maybe I'll pick up} something nice for {partner} on the way home.
{partner} {will|is going to} ask how my day went. {What do I even say|I'll make something up}.
{Wonder what|I bet} {partner} is doing right now.
Home to {partner} tonight. {That's the good part of the day|Best part of the day, honestly}.
familyPoly: {partner} and {partner2} both want dinner at mine. {The calendar on the fridge is war|We need a bigger table}.
Three birthdays to remember now. {partner} would never forgive me for forgetting.
{partner} says {partner2} took the last of the coffee. {I am staying out of it|Not my fight}.
People ask how it works with {partner} and {partner2}. {Patience and a good calendar|Same as anyone, but louder}.
familyLongDistance: {partner} is so far away. {Another letter tonight|I'll call when the rates drop}.
{Counting|Still counting} the days until I see {partner} again.
Long distance with {partner}. {The phone bill is a small tragedy|Worth every stamp}.
I kept the last postcard from {partner} in my {coat|wallet}.
familyAnniversary: {years} years with {partner} this month. {Where did they go|Feels like last week}.
Anniversary coming. {I still have not bought anything|Flowers, maybe. Or a proper dinner}.
{years} years and {partner} still laughs at my jokes. {Mostly|Sometimes}.
I should book a table for {partner} and me. {years} years deserves it.
familyPregnant: {The baby kicked again|Another kick}. {Someone is impatient|Hello to you too, little one}.
Everything aches and I {cannot stop smiling|am starving again}.
{partner} keeps asking if I need anything. {A new back, please|Pickles. Always pickles}.
Names. We still {do not|don't} have a name.
familyPartnerPregnant: {partner} is expecting. {I am going to be a parent|A parent. Me}.
Need to paint the small room before the baby comes.
{partner} wants pickles at three in the morning. {I will find pickles|Where does one find pickles at three}.
{Am I ready for this|Nobody is ready for this}. {Deep breath|One day at a time}.
familyNewborn: {child} woke up {four|five} times last night. {I have forgotten what sleep is|Coffee. Now}.
{child} grabbed my finger today and would not let go.
Nappies, bottles, nappies. {child} runs this house now.
{Is it normal|Surely it's normal} for {child} to cry this much? {I'll ask the doctor|Everyone says so}.
familyChildren: {child} has a school play next week. {I must not forget|Front row, I promised}.
{child} asked me why the sky is blue. {I said magic|I said ask your teacher}.
Need to pick {child} up before the shops close.
{child} is growing so fast. {New shoes again|The trousers are already short}.
familyAdultChild: {child} never calls. {Busy, I suppose|I'll write instead}.
{Proud of|So proud of} {child}. Not that I'd say it out loud.
{child} has their own life now. {Strange feeling|Quiet house}.
I wonder if {child} is eating properly.
familyParents: {parent} would have something to say about this. {Always does|Never stops}.
{parent} is getting older. {I notice it more now|The stairs are harder for them}.
{parent}'s cooking. {Nothing beats it|I still can't make it the same}.
familySiblings: {sibling} still owes me money. {Since school|For years now}.
Haven't seen {sibling} in a while. {Should call|Must write}.
{sibling} and I fought like cats as kids. {Now I miss it|Now we get on}.
familyBreakup: {Still can't believe|Hard to believe} it's over with {ex}.
I keep setting two cups out. {Habit|Stupid habit}.
{ex} {took the good pan|kept the records}. {Fine|Of course they did}.
Maybe being alone {for a while|again} is not so bad.
familyWidowed: {ex} would have liked today. {The weather was theirs|It was their kind of day}.
The house is so quiet without {ex}.
I still talk to {ex} sometimes. {Nobody needs to know|It helps}.
{ex}'s coat is still by the door. {I can't move it|Not yet}.
familyMovedOut: New flat, {new walls|same me}. Moving out was {the right call|harder than it looked}.
I left the house to {ex}. {Boxes everywhere now|Half my things are still in boxes}.
First night in the new place. {Strange noises|The pipes knock}.
Starting again from a {spare room|single room}. {Could be worse|It's a start}.
familyPartnerAway: {partner} is away on a trip. {The bed is too big|The house is too quiet}.
{partner} sent a postcard. {Wish I was there|Looks warm}.
{partner} back soon. {Must tidy up before then|Better hide the dishes}.
Cooking for one while {partner} is away. {Toast again|Soup again}.
familyParentalLeave: Parental leave. {Harder than any shift|Nobody told me it was a double shift}.
Home with {child} all day. {Every day is Monday|I've learned every lullaby}.
Work feels like another life. {child} is my job now.
{A nap|Ten minutes of quiet}. That's all I ask.
familyRefugeeKin: No letter from {kin} this month. {The camps have no post|I hope they're safe}.
{kin} fled the Horde with {nothing|one suitcase}. I should send money.
{kin} says the camp is cold at night. {I'll send blankets|I'll send a coat}.
When will {kin} be able to go home?
kidChild: {I want|Can I have} an ice cream!
{parent} said I can play until dinner!
I don't want to go to school tomorrow.
workSick: Off work sick. {The ceiling and I are old friends now|Tea and blankets}.
{Doctor says rest|Rest, they said}. {Easier said than done|I'm bored already}.
Hope they're managing without me at work. {Probably fine|Probably not}.
workUnemployed: Another day without work. {The papers have nothing|Nothing in the listings}.
Rent is due and {nothing|not a coin} coming in.
I used to complain about my job. {What I'd give|I'd take it back now}.
{Maybe|Perhaps} I should try another town. There's nothing here.
workAfterShift: Shift done. {My feet|My back} {hate me|are finished}.
Another day at the {job}, another few coins.
travelAway: {place} is lovely, but I miss my own bed.
{Must send|Should send} a postcard home from {place}.
Everything in {place} costs twice as much. {Tourist prices|Of course}.
A few more days in {place}, then home.
travelOnRoad: {Still hours|Hours yet} until {place}. {My legs are stiff|Should have brought a book}.
On the road to {place}. {I hope the room is booked|Fingers crossed for the weather}.
{place} by nightfall, {if the road holds|with luck}.
travelEmigrate: {Maybe it's time|It might be time} to leave {country} for good.
They say there's work abroad. {Nothing is keeping me here|What's left for me here}?
I've been looking at maps again. {Somewhere else|Anywhere else}.
If things don't improve by spring, I'm packing.
travelNewcomer: Still getting used to this town. {The streets all look the same|I get lost every day}.
I miss home. {The food, mostly|The people, mostly}.
Nobody here knows my name yet. {That will change|Give it time}.
New town, new start. {Fingers crossed|Let's see}.
warOurs: {We're at war with|Still fighting} {enemy}. {When will it end|How long this time}?
They're calling up more men against {enemy}. {I hope not my street|Not again}.
{power} and {enemy}. {More funerals|More ration cards}, that's all war brings.
Every news bulletin is about {enemy} now.
warFront: {enemy} wants {country}. {They'll have to take it|Over my dead body}.
If the front moves, {country} is next. {I should pack a bag|Keep the cellar stocked}.
The guns over the border {kept me up|woke the dog} again.
warFar: {power} and {enemy} are at it again. {Far from here, thankfully|Glad it's not us}.
Saw the war news from {power}. {Terrible|Poor souls}.
{power} against {enemy}. {Prices will go up here too|It'll be in our bread prices by winter}.
Someone should stop {power} and {enemy} before it spreads.
warPeace: Peace with {enemy}, finally. {I'll believe it when I see it|Let's hope it holds}.
The ONU actually did something. {First time for everything|Miracles happen}.
The soldiers are coming home from the {enemy} front.
A peace signed on paper. {Paper burns|Better than nothing}.
hordeFleeing: We left {from} with {what we could carry|nothing but the coats on our backs}.
The goblins took {from}. {I can still hear the drums|I keep seeing the smoke}.
{Just keep walking|Keep moving}. Anywhere the Horde isn't.
hordeCamp: Another night in the camp. {The tent leaks|The wind never stops}.
Queue for water, queue for bread. {Camp life|This is life now}.
The camp children play goblins and humans. {Humans always lose|I can't watch}.
{from} is only a few days away, and it might as well be the moon.
hordeSettled: {We have|I have} a roof here now, but it isn't {from}.
People here are kind, mostly. {Some of them stare|Some of them don't}.
I still set my watch to {from} time.
One day I'll take the train back to {from}. {One day|Someday}.
hordeReturned: Home in {from} again. {The house is still standing|Half the house is still standing}.
The goblins are gone from {from}. {Their smell isn't|The graffiti isn't}.
Back in {from}. {Neighbours I never thought I'd see again|Empty streets, but ours}.
hordeIntegrated: The goblins leave me be {if I pay the tithe|as long as I work}. {It's a life|Could be worse}.
I've learned enough Goblin to haggle. {They respect that|Mostly}.
The chief says humans are useful. {I intend to stay useful|Useful is safe}.
{Grubroot stew again|Beetle bread again}. You get used to it.
hordeUnder: {country} belongs to the Horde now. {Keep your head down|Don't look them in the eye}.
Goblin banners on the town hall. {I can't get used to it|Every morning it's a shock}.
They say the Horde will be pushed out of {country}. {They say a lot|Who says}?
Curfew at dusk. The goblins like the dark.
hordeFear: If the Horde comes over the border, {where do we even go|we run}.
Goblins spotted near the pass again. {I've locked the shutters|I sleep with a poker}.
My cousin says the Horde eats {horses|dogs}. {I believe it|Probably true}.
Every drum I hear, I think it's them.
playWon: Won at {game}! {Drinks on me|Knew my luck would turn}!
{game}, and I beat it. {Still got it|Not bad at all}.
playLost: Lost at {game} again. {Rigged|It's rigged, I swear}.
{game} ate my money. {Never again|Until next time}.
I was so close at {game}. {So close|Almost}!
fightInjured: {Bandages again|More bandages}. {Should see a healer|Should see a doctor}.
I'll have a scar from this one.
fightWitness: {Did you see that|Did you see} fight? {Terrifying|Unbelievable}.
Monsters in the street again. {Where are the guards|Nobody's safe}.
{I'm keeping my distance|I'm staying well back}.
crimeWanted: {Keep your head down|Walk normally}. {Nobody's looking|Nobody knows}.
Every uniform makes my stomach turn.
{Maybe|Perhaps} a new town and a new name.
That poster doesn't even look like me.
foodAte: That {item} {hit the spot|was just what I needed}.
{Eating|Ate} {item} on the go again. {No time to sit|Busy day}.
{item}. Not a proper meal, but it'll do.
Could have done with a second {item}.
specHoned: Getting better at {spec}. {Practice pays|All that practice}.
Someone asked me for help with {spec}. Me!
I've got a knack for {spec}, it turns out.
creedDoubt: Maybe the {creed} people have a point. {Just maybe|Don't tell anyone}.
I used to laugh at {creed}. {Now I'm not so sure|Now I'm reading their pamphlets}.
{Can't stop thinking|Keep thinking} about what they said about {creed}.
What if I've been wrong all along?
electionSoon: {days} days to the {election}. {party} or {rival}? {Still undecided|Hard call}.
{Posters everywhere|Leaflets in every letterbox}. The {election} is close.
{party} promises the moon again. {rival} promises it cheaper.
I'll vote. {I always vote|Somebody has to}. Just not sure for whom.
electionWeek: The {election} is this week. {party} is ahead in the polls, they say.
{rival} could still pull it off. {Polls lie|The polls were wrong last time}.
Which polling station is mine? {Must check|The school, I think}.
Everybody's arguing about the {election}. {Even the baker|Even my mother}.
electionDay: Voting day! {Queue at the school already|Off to the booth}.
Voted. {Now the long wait|Now we wait for the count}.
electionResult: {winner} in charge now. {Let's see what they do|Promises, promises}.

kinPartners: {Dinner at home tonight|Shall we cook together tonight}, {b}?
Only if I'm not doing the dishes.
{a}, you left the lights on again.
I left them on for you.
kinPartnersFight: {Then hear me|No, you're waiting to talk}.
Out. {Is that a crime|Do I need a permit}?
{The bills|The rent}, {a}. We need to talk about money.
kinPartnersMakeUp: {Me too|I'm sorry too}. I said things.
Agreed. {At least until Tuesday|Until the next time}.
kinAnniversary: I'd do every one of them again.
You remembered! {I thought you'd forget|I booked a table}.
kinParentChild: {Lovely|Wow}! Don't put it in your mouth.
Hold my hand when we cross, {b}.
kinParentChildScold: {b}! What did I say about running?
I don't want to go home!
{We're going now|Five more minutes, then home}.
kinParentAdultChild: When are you coming for Sunday lunch?
kinSiblings: Remember when we {broke the window|hid in the attic}, {b}?
kinNewborn: {Is that a smile|Was that a laugh}? {Clever little thing|Look at you}!
kidStranger: Hello! {What's your name|Are you a giant}?
{I'm {a}|Just a grown-up}. Where are your parents?
Careful where you run, little one.
aboutPartner: {partner} and I are {repainting the kitchen|planning a holiday}.
{Good|Busy, but good}. Always asking after you.
{partner} cooked last night. {Burned|Nearly burned} the house down.
aboutPoly: {partner} and {partner2} are fighting over the good armchair.
Doesn't it get complicated, with {partner} and {partner2}?
aboutChildren: Last week it was a baker.
{Takes after you|Takes after the other one}.
aboutNewborn: {child} kept us up all night again.
{I'll tell you when I know|About eighteen years}.
aboutBreakup: If you need a drink, I'm here.
aboutWidowed: {I'm so sorry|They were a good soul}.
Thank you. The days are long.
aboutParents: {parent} wants me over for Sunday lunch again.
{Stubborn as ever|The knees are bad, the tongue is fine}.
aboutRefugeeKin: {kin} is in a camp since the Horde came.
{One letter|Nothing yet}. The post is slow from the camps.
aboutMovedOut: {The pipes knock|Quiet}. It's mine, at least.
topicWar: Did you hear the news from the {enemy} front?
{I try not to|Every day}. It's bad.
They're drafting again for the war with {enemy}.
{My cousin got a letter|Not my boy, please}.
topicWarFront: I've packed a bag, just in case.
{Me too|Smart}. The front is too close.
topicElection: Who are you voting for? {party} or {rival}?
{days} days left. {party} will win, you'll see.
topicElectionResult: {winner} won. {Can you believe it|Of course they did}.
topicUnemployed: {Try the docks|Try the market}. They hire.
Any luck with the job hunt?
{No|Not yet}. The savings are running out.
topicRefugee: I came from {from} when the goblins took it.
Every day. The bread, the river, all of it.
topicIntegrated: The goblin overseer gave me a day off.
How do you stand living under them?
topicHordeFear: Goblins seen near the border again.
If the Horde comes, where do we go?
topicTrip: {Expensive|Wonderful}. {Glad to be home|Want to go back}.
topicNewcomer: Welcome. {The bakery on the corner is the best|Avoid the tavern pie}.
Takes a year. Then you're a local.
topicFight: {A scratch|Just bruises}. Should see the other thing.
topicConversion: They make sense, some of it.

partner: {partner} would like you. {Everyone does|They like everybody}.
My {partner} is waiting at home. {Can't be long|Mustn't be late}.
{partner} and I have been together {years} years. {Still going|Still arguing about the thermostat}.
poly: {partner} and {partner2} keep me busy. {Two anniversaries|Double the birthdays}.
I share a home with {partner} and {partner2}. {Loud house|Never lonely}.
longDistance: {partner} lives far off. {Letters every week|The phone bill is shocking}.
I see {partner} only now and then. Makes every visit count.
anniversary: {years} years with {partner} this month. {Don't let me forget flowers|I need a present}.
Our anniversary is soon. {partner} thinks I've forgotten.
pregnant: The baby is due soon. {Can you tell|I'm enormous}.
{partner} and I are expecting. {Terrified|Thrilled}, in equal measure.
partnerPregnant: {partner} is expecting. I'm going to be a parent!
We're painting the nursery. {partner} picked yellow.
newborn: My little {child} is {only months old|brand new}. I haven't slept since.
{child} has the loudest cry in the street, I swear.
children: My {child} is at school right now. {Hopefully learning something|Hopefully behaving}.
{child} wants to be just like you when they grow up. {Adventurers|Heroes}, the lot of you.
adultChild: My {child} is all grown up. {Never calls, of course|Doing well for themselves}.
{child} left home last year. The house is so quiet.
parents: My {parent} would talk your ear off. {Old stories|War stories}.
I look after {parent} these days. {They'd hate me saying so|Stubborn as a mule}.
siblings: My {sibling} and I don't talk much. {Old quarrel|Long story}.
{sibling} would like you. {They love travellers|They'd ask a thousand questions}.
breakup: {ex} and I split up. {Still sore|Don't ask}.
I'm single again since {ex}. {Taking it slow|Enjoying the quiet}.
widowed: I lost {ex} a while back. {Some days are better|You carry it}.
{ex} would have liked you. They liked everybody.
partnerAway: {partner} is away on a trip. {The house is too quiet|I'm eating toast every night}.
{partner} sends postcards from their trip. {Showing off|Rubbing it in}.
refugeeKin: My {kin} fled the Horde. {They're in a camp now|I send what I can}.
If you pass the camps, ask for {kin}. Tell them I'm thinking of them.

child: {name}, {home by dinner|stay where I can see you}!
